claims.claim_text: Affirm has a material commercial / installment-financing relationship with Amazon.com Services LLC and Amazon Payments, Inc., evidenced by the Amended and Restated Installment Financing Services Agreement (dated Nov 10, 2021) with four subsequent amendments through Oct 25, 2024, plus a warrant arrangement (Second Replacement Warrant dated Feb 14, 2025) to purchase Class A Affirm common stock issued to Amazon.com Services LLC.
claims.rationale: Named partner (Amazon) + specific written agreements filed as exhibits. Per Calibration Heuristic 7, material BNPL integration with a Fortune-1 retailer should appear in Amazon's own SEC filings as a counterparty/commercial agreement reference or in pay-method disclosures.

claims.claim_text: Affirm has a Global Customer Installment Program Agreement with Shopify Inc. dated February 14, 2025 (filed as exhibit 10.10 in a 10-Q dated May 9, 2025), implying a continuing material commercial relationship with Shopify as a commerce-platform partner. Shopify is referenced both as a strategic counterparty and historic investor (warrants).
claims.rationale: Named platform partner with specific dated agreement. Calibration Heuristic 7 — material BNPL platform relationships should appear in Shopify's 10-K/10-Q (partner/payment disclosures or related-party).

claims.claim_text: Affirm describes Apple Pay as an early-stage / actively developing commercial partner ('our continued success also is dependent on our ability to successfully grow and develop relationships with our commercial partners, particularly early-stage relationships with large e-commerce retailers and platforms such as Apple Pay'). Implies that Apple Pay is a material distribution channel for Affirm pay-over-time loans.
claims.rationale: Named tier-1 partner (Apple) — per Heuristic 7, a material consumer-payment integration with Apple Pay should be disclosable. The filing itself qualifies it as 'early-stage', so counterparty disclosure may be limited.

claims.claim_text: Affirm relies on Celtic Bank, Lead Bank, and Cross River Bank as originating bank partners — 'We currently rely on Celtic Bank and Lead Bank to originate substantially all of the loans facilitated through our platform.' Cross River Bank also provides the FDIC-insured high-yield Affirm Money savings account.
claims.rationale: Named bank partners with quantitative dependency. Calibration Heuristic 7 — material bank-partner relationships should appear in the bank's filings (though Celtic and Lead and Cross River are private/state-chartered, so EDGAR coverage is limited). Test by full-text search for cross-references.

claims.claim_text: For fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, Affirm facilitated consumer purchases of $36.7 billion in GMV across approximately 377,000 active merchants, with three loan product offerings (Pay-in-X, 0% APR installment, interest-bearing). Pay-in-X represented 14% of GMV, 0% APR 13%, and interest-bearing 72% of GMV.
claims.rationale: Quantified GMV claim — this is gross merchandise volume, NOT Affirm net revenue (Calibration Heuristic 3/9). Internal to filing; M-source verification is limited because GMV is not registry-published. The number itself is on the 10-K so this is a representation-of-fact claim with very narrow external verifiability. EXPECT UNVERIFIABLE.

claims.claim_text: Affirm achieved its first reported full-year GAAP net income — net income of $52.2 million for FY2025 (vs net loss of $517.8M FY2024 and $985.3M FY2023). Total revenue $3.22B (39% growth). Liquidity: $2.2B cash + securities; $5.2B available funding-debt capacity; $330M revolver undrawn. Convertible senior notes outstanding: $248.7M (2026 Notes 0%) and $920M (2029 Notes 0.75%); 2026 Notes mature Nov 15, 2026.
claims.rationale: Quantified financial-results / capital-structure claims. Going-concern / covenant-breach calibration heuristic 10 — Affirm explicitly states 'we were in compliance with all applicable covenants' and shows turning profitable, so distress signals appear ABSENT (positive). 2026 Notes maturity is a known near-term refinancing event.

claims.claim_text: Affirm's proprietary risk model has been built / calibrated on data from approximately 343 million loans. The company emphasizes 'machine learning, artificial intelligence, cloud-based technologies' and an 'AdaptAI' AI-powered personalized promotion platform as core competitive advantages.
claims.rationale: Subjective AI/ML claim (Heuristic 8). Test patent registry for any backing. Per cohort calibration, fintech is patent-light; expect low count. SEVERE only on Nikola-pattern (zero patents but headline AI claim).

claims.claim_text: Affirm sponsors an asset-backed-securitization program through master trust(s); as of June 30, 2025, $4.85B in notes issued by securitization trusts is outstanding, with $7.8 billion in loans held by third-party investors / unconsolidated VIEs and $8.7M repurchase liability accrued. The aggregate outstanding balance of $7.8B with the small repurchase liability implies low realized rep-and-warranty breach rates.
claims.rationale: Securitization issuance is publicly reportable via EDGAR (ABS-EE, FWP, 10-D filings). Programs sponsored by 'Affirm' (Affirm Asset Securitization Trust, AFFRM xxx-x series) should be searchable on EDGAR full-text.
